text:
lee: Ran the quickstart onboarding stress test with token TTL=4s and hit a big pile-up of retries after auth rotate. Multiple identical create calls slipped through.

tara: Ugh. Is this the SDK issuing immediate retries after refresh or something upstream?

lee: SDK. Timeline snippet:
```
12:00:00 request id=1 auth=tok_old -> 401
12:00:00 onAuthRefresh started
12:00:00 onAuthRefresh done -> tok_new
12:00:00 SDK retried id=1 immediately (no jitter) -> 429
12:00:00 SDK retry restarted backoff counter -> retried fast again -> duplicate resource
```

nate: Sounds like a parity bug: some SDKs preserve the backoff state across token refresh, some reset it. If many clients rotate simultaneously you get a retry storm.

tara: Short-term fixes: 1) Make SDKs preserve backoff attempt_count across onAuthRefresh (parity). 2) Add a tiny randomized jitter for immediate post-refresh retries (suggest 20-200ms). 3) Update quickstart README to recommend Idempotency-Key for create endpoints.

lee: Also: add a small CI scenario that simulates mass refresh + 50 clients and asserts duplicates <1%.

build-bot: Deploy queued: branch "fix/preserve-backoff-jitter" will run in staging at 2026-06-10T02:00Z.

nate: I'll add a unit test in JS asserting backoff state unchanged after onAuthRefresh resolves.

tara: I'll update quickstart and add a log line showing attempt_count/next_delay to help future triage.

lee: Filed INFR-8702 with logs, repro, and the three suggested mitigations. Marking P2.

nate: Thanks — will watch staging run and post results here.
